context: An elderly couple reflects on years of small daily routines
purpose: Teach: ひとつひとつ/案の定/暫く/流石/ずーっと/飼っ/つづける/掛かる

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: もう五十年か…毎朝、君が淹れてくれるお茶をずーっと飲んできたなぁ。
lines.en: Fifty years already... I've been drinking the tea you brew every morning for so long.
lines.style: Soft, wistful tone, gentle pace, reflective masculine warmth, slight smile audible in voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ふふ、あなたも毎晩、庭の植木をひとつひとつ見て回ってましたよね。
lines.en: Heh, and you used to walk the garden every night, checking each plant one by one.
lines.style: Warm, fond laugh under the words, unhurried elderly feminine tone, tender remembrance.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: あの猫もそうだ。拾ってきた日、案の定お前が「飼っていきましょう」って言い出して。
lines.en: And that cat too. The day we found him, sure enough you said, "Let's keep him."
lines.style: Playful teasing tone, gentle chuckle, affectionate elderly husband cadence, easy nostalgia.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: だってあの子、雨の中で暫くじっと座ってたのよ。流石に放っておけなくて。
lines.en: Well, the poor thing sat in the rain for quite a while. I really couldn't just leave him.
lines.style: Soft defensive but warm, slightly higher pitch on memory, kind-hearted grandmother tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そういう小さな習慣をつづけることって、思ったより時間が掛かるもんだなぁ。
lines.en: Keeping up those little habits really takes more time than you'd think.
lines.style: Thoughtful, slow exhale before the line, philosophical elderly reflection, low and calm.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: でも、その積み重ねが今の私たちなんですよ、あなた。
lines.en: But all those little things piled up are what made us who we are today, dear.
lines.style: Tender, voice softening on "あなた," gentle conviction, lifetime of affection in delivery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだな。明日も、お茶と庭と猫と…ひとつずつ、また始めようか。
lines.en: You're right. Tomorrow too — tea, the garden, the cat — let's begin again, one by one.
lines.style: Quiet, contented resolve, gentle smile in voice, soft fade at the end, peaceful.
